exact_definition_clause: Comparisons of these embedded diagrams allow **orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms**: an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of $S^3$ carrying the two handlebodies, their oriented Heegaard surface, the two attaching systems, the ordered $w,z$ points, and the two simultaneously boundary-parallel arc systems to the corresponding data. Equivalently one may specify the surface isomorphism together with its compatible collared extensions over both handlebodies carrying those arcs. The attaching systems are carried as systems; reordering their curve factors induces the corresponding product identification. Such a comparison transports the represented oriented knot and any specified Seifert surface as well. For analytic data, it transports $j$, the surface area form, all chosen divisor neighborhoods and $J_t$ by the induced symmetric-product diffeomorphism. The comparison maps on generators and disk classes are their pushforwards under this map; compatibility with the count differential is a mathematical property to be proved. No identity action is part of this convention, even when the ambient diffeomorphism is isotopic to the identity.
exact_before_theorem_sentence: Any two such diagrams are related by a finite sequence of these moves through admissible multipointed diagrams, preserving the represented oriented knot.
exact_after_theorem_sentences: Comparisons may apply the orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms of the pointed-data definition, carrying the ordered marked points, attaching systems and simultaneous boundary-parallel arcs, before or after the listed geometric moves. Their complex identifications are induced by pushforward of generators, disk classes and almost complex data, rather than by assuming an isotopy acts as the identity. Comparisons also allow the fixed-splitting arc normalizations in that definition before or after the listed moves, retaining the simultaneous bridge witnesses and all ordered marks. They leave the surface attaching and analytic data fixed, so their identification of the actual count operators is the identity; they do not assert a diffeomorphism of a tangential and transverse surface-knot pair. With these identifications, any two such diagrams are related by a finite sequence of the listed moves through admissible multipointed diagrams, preserving the represented oriented knot.
